table.column: Choose the app you'd like to launch from the list below.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Even after civilization has crumbled, some of the GPS satellite network remains operational.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Even after civilization has crumbled, some of the GPS satellite network remains operational.

table.name: encounters
table.column: You're outside the DSB Gate 11 microbranch, now empty and locked.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Under normal circumstances, picking a lock in plain view on some busy sidewalk is a dumb move.
Under these circumstances, it still is. You work your magic on the lock, but by the time you're seated at the terminal, someone outside is already on their mobile. Probably talking to the police.
There's no sign of the teller yet, but you're betting your time here is limited.
Damn that good Samaritan.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Wait for the teller to leave.

You find a position with a good vantage point, and stare at the booth like a psycho for a while.
The booth doesn't garner a lot of foot traffic, which might explain why there are so few of them around town.
As you're waiting, you think she spots you, but you can't be sure. Waiting a bit longer, she starts talking on her mobile, and glances your way, looking down again when she sees you.
It appears you've been made.
As you hurry down the sidewalk, faint sirens can be heard echoing through the canyon of skyscrapers.

table.name: encounters
table.column: You've got access to the computer now, but not much time. The threatening of a bank employee is sure to be high on the police priority list.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You are taken to collect your things. "Don't forget anything. Abandoned items will be destroyed," the guard warns.
Better make sure you empty that locker while you have the chance.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You steel your nerves, and bolt, veering left immediately.
A flash of red emits from the skybike's undercarriage, and your body is painted in a flickering cross-hatched pattern.
You hear a beep, followed by a loud "pow!"
Something slams into you, and you collapse instantly, muscles seizing uncontrollably. Unable to move, see, or even hear straight, the world is an agonizing blur as you flop on the asphalt.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You steel your nerves, and bolt, veering left immediately.
A flash of red emits from the skybike's undercarriage, and your body is painted in a flickering cross-hatched pattern.
You hear the engines change pitch as the vehicle reorients, a beep, followed by a loud "pow!"
Something smacks against the ground near your feet, flashing arcs of electricity as it skitters.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Well, this is familiar. You're back in the beige fortress, awaiting processing by DMC Perimeter Services.
Same old ceiling tiles. Same old filing cabinets. Same old missing persons...

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're escorted from the interview area, and brought into an on-site clinic, where you're strapped to a table, and anesthetized.
When you wake, you're on a bench in a painted cinder block room, leaning against a corner. Both your head and right shoulder ache. A piercing bleep fills the room as an intercom comes to life.
"You have been charged as follows: -First-degree criminal trespassing -Unauthorized access to a computer with intent to commit an offense -Fraud and misuse of visas -Conspiracy to defraud the city of Detroit -Consorting with a known felon -Failure to disclose personal information"

table.name: encounters
table.column: DMC Questioning - Exile I to II

This time, when the case handler arrives, there's no talking. Just scribbling notes, cross-checking a nearby monitor, and a stern glance telling you you're not worth the effort.
A guard grabs your shoulder, and pushes you into the cinder block room with the blaring speakerphone.
A voice blares, "Repeated violation of exile order is cause for term of sentence to be extended by 2 years. Subsequent violations may be subject to penalties including capital punishment, at the discretion of the arresting officer."
A door on the opposite wall buzzes, and swings open to the familiar muddy streets outside the DMC walls.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
At the front of the line, the guard motions you closer. A moment of pregnant silence precedes a satisfying chirp, and the monitor flashes.
"Visitor Pass N6MAB11324 Authorized."
You wait for them to let you pass but the guard speaks something to his comms. Another guard arrives and places a heavy-gloved hand on your shoulder. "Alright, buddy, let's go."
You're led to a gray door at the base of the south buttress, alongside a thin slit of mirrored windows.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You steel your nerves, and bolt, veering left immediately.
A flash of red emits from the skybike's undercarriage, and your body is painted in a flickering cross-hatched pattern.
You hear a beep, followed by a loud "pow!"
Something slams into you, and you stagger a few steps as muscles clench near the impact.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You steel your nerves, and bolt, charging directly under the skybike.
A flash of red emits from its undercarriage, and your body is painted in a flickering cross-hatched pattern.
You hear the engines change pitch as the vehicle reorients, a beep, followed by a loud "pow!"
Something smacks against the ground near your feet, flashing arcs of electricity as it skitters.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Positioning yourself for optimal viewing, you await the teller's login.
However, a shout startles you out of your vigil. The technician's checklist goes on hold as she notices your staring, and starts speaking into her earpiece.
The teller's been alerted, too, and is standing up.
Things are about to get pretty hot here. Time to jet.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
As you turn to leave the market, you hear a bell ringing, its clanging reverberating through the honeycomb of shipping containers. You soon see angry sprawlers marching your way. You recognize one of them, the butcher that was buying meat. He heads towards you, scattergun in hand.
Everyone else stops, turning. Craning their necks to see around the crowd at the commotion.
"Flesh peddler!" he shouts. "Cannibal!"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
And the silence here is deafening. No birds, nor critters. Not even insects. Nothing stirs in this caustic swamp of destruction.
Nothing lives here.
Or at least, nothing should.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Hey!" a voice booms. The butcher's voice.
"Didn't I tell you?" The market quiets to a murmur.
"I done told you, didn't I?" He points his knife at you. "I ever see you and human meat together, under this roof..." and he draws the knife across his neck, in a cutting motion.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Oh," he says, distracted. Then, he becomes more animated.
"Oh! Ya mean the hot bricks! Sure! Sure. Think I've got a spare 'round here..." Boxes are pushed about. Papers displaced.
"Whatchu got ta offer?"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Turning back to you, he asks, "How about ol' Gerty. Think ya can help 'er?"
He adds, "Be a reeal help, you know?"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Well, you've got this...thing. It's a long shot, but maybe it'd draw that bike's attention?
You locate a crude power switch, take a deep breath, and flip...

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The meat has a powerful, mostly pleasant taste. Combined with the sauces, it's spicy, salty, and sweet. Probably engineered that way.
And the texture is homogenous and unoffensive. No fibers, fats, nor bone.
Though after a few bites, you can see where the veggies come in. Roughage, something to chew on, and actual nutrients are not amiss here.
Still, it helps fill the pit inside, and you can see how this might become a habit for locals.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
A crispy, salty-sour shell gives way to a softer, more flavor-neutral center. It's a pleasant sensation, the initial flavor and crunch.
However, the plate is gone almost too soon, and you're left feeling about as satisfied as if you'd eaten the equivalent volume of cheese puffs.
At least this was healthier.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The roast isn't bad, in fact. Gamey, to be sure. And a bit milder than the stuff one finds "out there".
There's some stringiness and gristle to it, too. Less desirable in days past, but proof you have actual meat in this case. Meat of what, you're probably better off not knowing.
The cabbage is actually a nice touch, despite its rank among cheap nutrients. Fresh-cooked veggies are not common fare these days.
You gulp down the last bites, and get your bearings again.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're escorted from the interview area, and brought into an on-site clinic, where you're strapped to a table, and anesthetized.
When you wake, you're on a bench in a painted cinder block room, leaning against a corner. Both your head and right shoulder ache. A piercing bleep fills the room as an intercom comes to life.
"You have been charged as follows: -First-degree criminal trespassing -Unauthorized access to a computer with intent to commit an offense -Fraud and misuse of visas -Conspiracy to defraud the city of Detroit -Consorting with a known felon -Failure to disclose personal information"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Well, guess I'll keep lookin'," he concedes. "Least you ain't one of those bastards try ta steal my stuff. And no guvmint agent, neither!"
His jovial outburst sobers. "You jus' watch out fer them, I tell ya'."
Bob holds the door open for you, as a sign of good faith. You still can't help stepping hurriedly through the antechamber, though.
Once outside, you cast a final glance over your shoulder, and then continue down the ravine.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Locked storage sheds are a good sign. Somebody thinks there's something valuable inside, and nobody else has been able to remove it yet.
The question is, can you get past the lock?

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Yo I ain't got time fa' this." His words come fast and fluid.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Hey, man, I'm not lookin' for no trouble."

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Hey, man, you inbound or outbound?" His head is on a swivel, glancing to and fro as he talks.

table.name: encounters
table.column: He gives you a sidelong look. "What now? What you want?"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Mashugana."
"What?" Was that even English?
"Mashugana, mashugana, mashugana. I ain't talkin' to you. Go."
"Away."

table.name: encounters
table.column: Ask why he doesn't sell it himself.

"Any reason you're not selling this yourself? Seems an awful shame to give up all that profit."
"Oh, haha," he starts. "I'm not heading in there a while yet. You know. I just need a few things, and I'm not heading in there for a while."
"Besides, you're heading in anyways, right? You're helpin' me out, and you get a little somethin' extra. Everybody wins," he chuckles.
"So, whaddya say?"

table.name: encounters
table.column: "This better be good, yo," he says, impatiently.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"How's it goin'?" He continues before you can answer.
"Look, I appreciate you taking it easy on me and all. There's enough shit going on out here without all the fighting. So, thanks, bro." His thanks seem pretty earnest.
"But I got something I need to take care of right now. I'll catch you later." And with that, he heads off purposefully.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Hooooo! Fresh meat off the farm," she cackles.
"This place is gonna pick you cleeeean," she adds, walking past you.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Well, well, well. Dis my knight in shinin' armor? Or my dark prince?"

table.name: encounters
table.column: "You just hold it right there," she warns. "That's close enough."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"I jus' have two words for you, "she says, then sticks her face forward as if transmitting thoughts into your mind.
Satisfied, she walks away.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Man, I wish these bags had a condition gauge on them or somethin'. You be walkin' along one day, and 'pow!' Thing just falls apart!"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"I've had nighmares nicer than this place," she huffs.
She doesn't seem interested in waiting for a response.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "I hear they found a cheater up at Zom Zom's. Hooo-boy, that was a party!"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Whoever decided that dogs needed to be bigger and walk on two legs needs to DIE!"
She just storms past you.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"...was at the fifty-five by the two-oh." He stops speaking into a radio, disappointed at the interruption.
"What you need?"

table.name: encounters
table.column: He laughs loudly. "Ho ho, look! This meat talks!"

table.name: encounters
table.column: "I ain't talkin' to no asshole...I ain't talkin' to no asshole..." he repeats into the air, ignoring you as he passes.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Can't be doin' this, man. I gots stuff to do." He continues on, purposefully.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Honey, I'm tired of walkin'," she admits.
Then, in a lower voice, "but I ain't *that* tired."

table.name: encounters
table.column: "I make it a point not to talk to strangers out here," she cautions. "So you just move along, and we don't need to bother each other none."

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Just you keep your nose clean, and we got no trouble," he spits as he glances at you for a couple of seconds.

table.name: encounters
table.column: How do I get into the DMC?

"What's it take to get through the gate?"
He responds to radio chatter coming from somewhere in his headgear, ignoring you for a moment.
"You gonna need a visitor pass," he recites. "Applications at the gate, and processing time is 6-10 months."
His radio pipes up again, and he starts walking away, listening.

table.name: encounters
table.column: What's the story with the swamp?

"What's the story with the swamp?"
"Chemical wash," he responds, quickly. "Nobody's permitted down there. Highly toxic."
"Yeah, but why?"
"Some crops got out of control back in the day. Had to burn them with chemicals."
Radio chatter pipes up, and he turns slightly from you. Then, he walks away, speaking back to his radio.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Any gangs I should be watching out for around here?"
The guard seems suddenly interested. "Yeah, definitely. Could be some crooked Sprawlers 'round, but gangs aren't unheard of around here, either." He looks past you.
"There are some religious loonies who call themselves Blue Frogs. Just stay away from them is all I can say. There are also tribals but if you see those then that means you are too far from the DMC. Then there is this group that call themselves Martha's Army. They seem to enjoy smashing electronics. Bad Muthas are the worst of 'em. Damn cannibals, you ask me. We get some Butcher Boys, too."
Looking back at you, "You just keep close to town, though, and you're better off."
A message over the radio calls him away.

table.name: encounters
table.column: "Police business," he holds up his hand, "coming through."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Minutes of silent traveling later, you begin to hear sounds. Not forest sounds, but people sounds. Tools being worked. A crack from a fire.
Voices startle you from your strained listening. Your captors are talking, but not in English. Not in anything you recognize.
One of them calls out, and a distant voice responds. It sounds like you're entering a camp of some kind. You smell wood burning. Your arrival causes a stir, and you stop moving for a moment.
More talking.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Your hunger sated, you lean back in the warmth of the room. The scent of dinner mingles with cedar and tobacco.
Despite the weight in your stomach, there is a sense of unrest within you.
Anxiety is pulling you toward the door. A fear is trying to convince you that every moment in here is threatening your existence.
But there is a part of you wanting to stay. Instinct is holding you fast.
You're not sure whether laziness and contentedness is putting you in danger, or if addiction is dragging you away from recovery.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're standing in the Anishinaabe Tribal Nation's gathering area, by the Great Fire.
Around you, you see an area where people are sharing a meal together. Just behind this area you see a small hut with prices set on a chalkboard, and a trader of goods just outside the hut.
Further away, you see a cluster of huts near a sweat lodge, where Joe, the Nooke Midewinini, tends to the sick and wounded.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The warrior just presses a finger to her lips, signaling silence.
Then, she turns her attention back to the area around you, seemingly stalking something.

table.name: encounters
table.column: She seems to be gauging the surroundings for a moment, but then she turns to you, satisfied there is no danger near.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"This is not the place for talking," he says, paying more attention to something beyond you.
"We may talk later."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
She considers your story.
"You should speak with Michelle Lavallee, our Ajijaak elder. She is interested in these things, and knows a lot about them."
She explains how to find her enclave.
"Just be respectful," she warns. "Our warriors are accustomed to troublemakers entering our lands."
With that, she gets back to her route. "Wiingezin, traveler."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The trading post seems to be a place where travelers resupply and offload items which may be of use to the Anishinaabe.
The goods inside the hut seem to be mostly food and items sold in bulk. It looks more like a storage area than a general store.
The trader outside the hut offers a variety of goods. A large portion of the inventory appears to be handmade items from local materials, and some scavenged goods.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You approach the long table, and find an open place on the bench.
The food here is plentiful, and appears to be a mix of roasted and dried meats, roasted corn or maize, baked squash, and beans.
There is also an assortment of berries and other fruit.
Overall, the meal is hearty, with diverse flavors of savory and sweet. It fills your stomach, briefly allowing your mind to wander from minute-to-minute survival.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
There is an indirect science to the medicine, as well. Having observed the animal world's interaction with nature, certain plants and animals have been singled out for their healing properties.
Bear root, boiled in water to extract the medicine, can have restorative effects. Some have even reported illnesses waning under its effects.
Chewing on the root and sipping the tannin tea, your body gains a newfound energy for combating illness.
You thank Joe for his time and his help, then leave the lodge.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The enclave has four lightly guarded gates. There isn't much traffic but the four of them are opened all the way. They probably really trust their sentries and patrols.
Which gate do you want to exit from?

table.name: encounters
table.column: He stops a moment, sizing you up. Once satisfied, his attention seems to return to the surroundings.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
She raises her hand with a smile.
"Catch anything good?"
"Boots," you reply.
"Ha ha, lucky!" She waves again as you part ways.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
At the front of the line, the guard motions you closer. A moment of pregnant silence precedes a satisfying chirp, and the monitor flashes.
"Visitor Pass N6MAA10816 Suspect Flagged: Detain for Questioning."
Your gut suddenly feels like a vacuum. The guard places a heavy-gloved hand on your shoulder. "Alright, buddy, let's go."
You're led to a gray door at the base of the south buttress, alongside a thin slit of mirrored windows.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're escorted from the interview area, and brought into an on-site clinic, where you're strapped to a table, and anesthetized.
When you wake, you're on a bench in a painted cinder block room, leaning against a corner. Both your head and right shoulder ache. A piercing bleep fills the room as an intercom comes to life.
"You have been charged as follows: -Assault on a Skycorps agent -Resisting arrest -Failure to disclose personal information"

table.name: encounters
table.column: DMC Questioning - Carrying most wanted visitor pass

By the time your case handler arrives, you've counted the ceiling tiles, grouped them into shades of beige, and created an elaborate conspiracy linking all the missing persons.
Your handler leads you to his cubicle, and you're subjected to a battery of tests, including face scan, retinal scan, DNA sampling, fingerprinting, and a blood sample.
The interview is something of a comedy, with questions like "What is your full name, address, and date of birth?"
The handler isn't amused, however. He then asks about the bracelet and where you found it. You tell him about the strange forest, the creature that lurked in it and the lady. You can't tell if he believes you but his interest in the bracelet is evident.

table.name: encounters
table.column: You decide not to mess with this place, and duck out of sight.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Your eyes adjust slowly to the dark indoors. The decay is pungent. Wood rot. Bodily fluids. The guard takes you to a lamp-lit room where a short, pudgy cultist squats on the ground, unmasked. Three frog-shaped sculptures sit around him. Pamphlets and posters litter the floor.
"Welcome, brother," the cultist says as he zips up his pants and hugs you. "Call me Rollo. The King is always delighted when one joins his flock. But before you see him, you must be pure.
"Choose, then. A trial of water, of fire, or," he says as a twisted grin joins his ears, "of light?"

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You feel wave after wave crash down, turning cotton into rubber over your face. You try not to gag. Struggle as you might, a brook trickles up your nose when you inhale and down your throat when you swallow. You wish death would just take that last step.
When it stops, the taste of filthy water lingers on your tongue. It's all you can do to stop the waters from rising again.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You don't count how many times the cultist pours water over your face. You don't count how many gulps of water you swallow just so you can breathe. You don't count the pleas you make, only how many times they're heard.
When the drowning is done, the light in the room has changed. A lantern flickers and you vomit a small puddle onto the decrepit floor.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The emptied cabinets against the walls and those forming two short rows in front of you lend the space some semblance of being a locker room. They keep Blue Frog paraphernalia here. Spares, most likely: gas masks, blue arm bands and sashes, and various other treasures like detached fingers.
On the far side, a Blue Frog gently bumps his head against the wooden boards sealing the window.
The doorway leads back out into the east wing.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Blue banners flood the northern hallway more than any other place you've seen in the stronghold, twisting and writhing against each other from gusts of wind that shouldn't be. The smell of stagnant air turns thick. Between the dead yet unbroken fluorescents tracking the ceiling, lanterns lead your eye to a central set of doors.
Cultist engravings run around the doorframe and spill onto the surrounding walls and floor like a fungal growth. It doesn't sound like anyone's inside. You look around before testing the doors.
They're locked.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Blue Frog banners draw you in as if curtains lifting on a stage. The auditorium swells before your eyes, its walls rounding out into the dark infinity on the other side, its ceilings breaching the heavens of the second floor. Hanging beneath the observation deck that circles the room, lanterns throw shadows far and wide.
At the center, in front of a dome structure mantled by a thousand candles, a man in lush blue robes stands on an examination chair like it's an unfit throne. His voice is like thunder.
"It was the Savior himself," the King cries, "who spoke to our Founder! Who told him of the Return! Who told him to believe! And do we believe, brothers and sisters?"
The crowd of Blue Frogs screams.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Ah, a visitor!" says a Blue Frog cultist squatting on the ground. "Have you come to reminisce with old Rollo, brother?"
It's a strange sight to come upon someone making a room their personal toilet. It's entirely different to see someone doing that while surrounded by three frog sculptures posing in the same way.
"The room where all of us are reborn," he looks around with pride. "This is good work."
Torn posters and pamphlets litter the floor. Upon a closer look, you see that they're for a treatment called ECT. The plastic-happy faces on them are terrifying.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Quickly pick the locked door and head inside.

You wonder why you went through all the trouble of picking the door lock and slipping inside. The room is mostly bereft not only of anything valuable, but even of character. No trophies, no weapons, no history. What few things there are congregate in the far corner, surrounding themselves with emptiness.
There does appear to be a safe, however, flanked by a mattress and a pot.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
There is little left to explore in this burnt, toxic swamp. This ruin, however, looks like it might have a few caches that escaped complete destruction.
Getting to them, however, is going to be a trick. Rubble threatens to collapse at the slightest touch, and caustic liquid pools here and there.
The good news? You suspect little scavenging competition in this blasted swamp.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You've stumbled across a crash site.
It looks like a hover truck went down here, crashing through trees and dirt, and scattering it nearby.
There's been a lot of damage in the impact and subsequent fire, but you may find some useful stuff in the wreckage.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You've stumbled across a crash site.
It looks like part of a hover convoy went down here. Vehicle wreckage and containers are spread over the crash site, and peek out of the swamp.
Fire, corrosion, and the crash have taken their toll, but you're betting few scavengers have been through this dismal swamp yet, so the pickings may be good.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You stop dead in your tracks when a scattering shadow appears before you, resolving its formlessness from thin air, making and unmaking itself along its fringes. Below a pale mask on what looks like its head, a bronze light burns. And there is fury in the light.
With a movement no human body could make, the wraith hurls something at you, then vanishes. You nearly fall back at the force, but manage to stay upright.
You look down. It's a crumpled gas mask with a broken beak.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Climbing over debris up the stairs, you reach a T intersection, with the living room opening up to your right. There is a musty smell up here, with a faint, sickening sweetness.
Across the living room, you see a hutch surrounded by broken dishes. And atop it, a silver urn.
You cross the moldy room to the hutch, retrieve the urn, and look closely at it. Doesn't seem like much, but to each there is a treasure.

table.name: encounters
table.column: If not you, then someone else will clean this place out. Better get started.

table.name: encounters
table.column: As you round a corner, you nearly miss it: a reinforced door inset into a brush-covered slope nearby. With the exception of a white button next to the door, there are no other signs of life nearby.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Elias was a bit of a strange man, I admit," Samantha says. "But he was good to us, and he was always so happy to see us. He could only come home once or twice a month, and for no more than a day or two at a time. But when he was here, he was really here, you know? And he never took his work home with him."
She pauses. "Then again, why would he? Being a medicine courier hardly seems that taxing."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
As the King of the Blue Frog cult lies dead at your feet, a blast of pallid light infests and dries the air with a sudden roar. You feel something coming from behind you. And you turn.
A surge of blackest shadow twists out of itself before you, swelling with such intensity that shards of darkness are shed from its being. A bone-white mask with hollow eyes crowns the being. An eerie yellow light glows beneath it, rumbling with rage.
An instant later, it folds upon itself and disappears.
When you can see your surroundings again, you find the King's body unmoved. A few feet away, a gas mask is torn in half, right down its beak.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Try to broker a deal for the Blue Rot materials.

The junk market might pay a nominal fee for biotech, but this sort of thing goes much further in the right hands.
Fortunately, you know just such a set of hands.
Once the guard has helped you get situated in the elevator, you begin the trundling passage to the upper floors.
Stepping off the lift, Hatter's already eyeing you up, to see what this is all about.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Hatter's guard informs you that Hatter's on important business right now, and isn't expected back soon.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Return to Hatter after being paid for big Blue Rot deal

Hatter's guards treat you differently now. Instead of the stand-offishness of yore, they greet you as if a regular.
"Mr. Kindred," he nods. "We haven't recieved any relevant news for you. Thanks for stopping by, though."

table.name: encounters
table.column: Hatter's guard informs you that Hatter's on important business right now, and won't be back until tomorrow.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Return to the room in the north wing.

You wonder why you went through all the trouble of picking the door lock and slipping inside. The room is mostly bereft not only of anything valuable, but even of character. No trophies, no weapons, no history. What few things there are congregate in the far corner, surrounding themselves with emptiness.
There does appear to be a safe, however, flanked by a mattress and a pot.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
It first seemed that the communal bathroom's lights had been turned off, but as you approach, you see a flickering outline along the inner fringes of the doorframe.
You stand in front of it, listening to the quiet click-click-click of the light- a testament to how quiet it is in here despite the space's potential for echoing.
You can't explain it, but you shiver when you reach for the door.
It's locked.

table.name: encounters
table.column: I want to burn Grayling down.

The woman holds still. "You're lying," she says, her voice steadier than the mist.
"No," you plead. "This base has to be destroyed. I have committed to that, and it is the only reason I've come here, dangerous as it is."
She eases forward, never pointing her gun away. You stand still.
When she's close enough that you can see the hazel of her eyes surrounded by blue and green dazzle facepaint, she asks: "Are you really telling the truth?"
You nod.
She all but drops her gun. "Oh, thank god."

table.name: encounters
table.column: As you approach, you can't help staring at his face paint. It looks like someone tested an entire shape stencil sheet on his face.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"You carryin'?" he asks, stopping a short distance away.
You look at him, confused.
"Tracking devices," he exhales. "Bugs. Hardware. Got anything switched on?"

table.name: encounters
table.column: "We move without *them* watching," he nods upward. He doesn't stop to talk.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Privacy is our greatest asset," he recites as he passes by you.
"Anonymity is our greatest weapon."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're in the parking lot of Gyges Cryo Facility, but everything looks disused and in disrepair. Plants have pushed their way through the pavement and over the facility.
Worst of all, nothing looks familiar. You don't remember this place, or even who you are. Your frustration mounts, but you catch it and put it in check. Might as well take a look around.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
The distant report of a gun disrupts your thoughts. You cock your head, listening, but it's over as quickly as it started.
Obviously you're not alone out here. Though that doesn't necessarily comfort you.
You snap out of it. "First things first," you tell yourself. "Let's make sure we've lost that...thing."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"These are dark times," she greets you.
You nod. "You could say that."
"Though," she adds, seizing upon your willingness to talk, "sometimes darkness can be on our side."

table.name: encounters
table.column: "You'll have to excuse our manners," she concedes. "Us conspiracy-types tend to wax poetic. Comes with the territory."

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Where there is security," she opines, "there is no liberty."
She doesn't stop to talk.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Privacy is our greatest asset," she recites as she passes by you.
"Anonymity is our greatest weapon!"

table.name: encounters
table.column: You cross the muddy street towards the old flophouse.

table.name: encounters
table.column: See if Hatter has any work for you.

You step off the familiar lift, and Hatter turns to look at you, finishing his conversation.
"Private call with a client, boys," Hatter says to his hired guns. "Don't worry if this one kills me; your pensions are nil either way."
He circles behind his desk. And when the guards shut the doors behind them, he says, "We have to talk."

table.name: encounters
table.column: Hatter's guard informs you that Hatter's on important business right now, and isn't expected back soon.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Once cheap and ubiquitous at roadside stops, these pocket roadmaps have become something of an archeological tool for modern scavengers.
You carefully unfold the giant leaf, and try to make sense of where you are.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're standing outside the "Last Chance" Canteen.
Originally named for its location on the outskirts of the Sprawl, locals often joke that the "Last Chance" Canteen is, in fact, a warning to prospective patrons.
Known for serving whatever is "available", as well as a few suspect staple dishes, the "Last Chance" is a venue for those hungry and not too fussy about their food's origins.
Still, the old fifth-wheel draws lines enough to keep its grills hot, so nobody must've died from their food.
Yet.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
"Didja know seagull's a land bird?" the cook shouts over the fans and sizzling. "Easy to catch, too!" he guffaws.
"Yeah, and easy to overcook," you add, under your breath.

table.name: encounters
table.column: What you get isn't far from what you imagined: smallish; amorphous; fried; tender.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Despite your inquiries, you fail to learn anything more about the non-committal stew.
The flavor is just as perplexing as the name. Better than dirty socks boiled in MSG, but only just. Still, it's a very filling meal.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Feeling more adventurous, you opt for the extra protein sprinkled over the mixed veggie bowl.
While the blackened, cornflake-like objects don't address the lack of flavor in the original dish, you can't argue that it doesn't change the texture.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
Being the safest dish on the menu, it's arguably the most popular. Not for lack of trying, though.
A mix of sprouts and shredded carrots, lettuce, and turnips fried in oil, if it had a flavor, you'd describe it as savory with a sweet-yet-pungent aftertaste.
If it had a flavor.

table.name: encounters
table.column: The food may be sketchy, but at least the bottled water is legit.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
St. James Parkade is what it sounds like: a pre-apocalypse parking garage. Except in this case, repurposed to berth humans. Someone had the bright idea to leave all the cars in a parking garage, hook them up to an unlicensed power tap, and charge occupancy by the night.
A patron could rent an open pickup if they're down on their luck (and own a sleeping bag). They could rent a hatchback if they have a little extra to spend on heat and shelter (and door locks). Or, if they have the taste for finer living, splurge for a full-size van with its own chem-toilet.
The rent also includes access to your very own storage space. There's a keypad on each door, so the storage rooms are protected by electronic locks. Fancy.
It's no Ritz Carlton. However, it's also not sleeping exposed to anyone who wanders by. And that's what counts.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
When you find your stall, there's a maroon pickup truck in it. The bed's more than big enough to stretch out, maybe for two or three people if you really wanted.
The cab, on the other hand, is pretty minimal. No sleeping in there, unless you're a fan of sore neck and back.
It'll do for a place to safely stash your stuff, though. And the parkade's roof at least stops the rain.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You find your assigned stall, and there's an emerald-colored hatchback there, covered in dust.
Inside, some of the seats have been removed, but the rear bed offers just enough room to stretch out.
There are no amenities inside. No blankets, TV, or running water. However, the old electric engine's been wired to the grid, so you have ample climate control and light. Combined with door locks and windows, this beats most beds you've made while in the wild.

table.name: encounters
table.column: Rent a full-size van for 24 hours - $120

When you arrive at your stall, you find a large, gray conversion van parked there.
With an extended roof, built-in porta-potty, and comfortable appointments, this is as top-of-the-line as you're gonna get in this place.
You toss your things inside, lock the doors behind you, and draw the curtains. With the heat just right, and the lights dimmed, you stretch out in your temporary mansion.

table.name: encounters
table.column:
You're alerted to the sound of a cart approaching. A guy in a hoodie pushes his cart to a nearby car, checks for occupants, and unlocks it. He makes quick work of taking anything of value left in the car, and throws trash into a big bin.
Then, he starts wheeling towards you. "Time's up, buddy."
Better get your stuff together and go, lest any of it end up on that cart.

Hardware/Software: If hardware/software is not switched on and unlocked, vendors will only pay the hardware's value as if it were empty. Items will then be appraised by a specialist, and resold at full price.
Items in Containers: If you can't afford the items inside a container, you are not allowed to pick the container up. Also, you can only empty out items you can afford from the containers.
Unidentified Items: Vendors will only pay a nominal fee for unidentified items. The items will then be identified and sold at full price.
When in doubt, verify the vendor's purchase price before surrendering items to them. All sales final!
